messages:
Sofia P: Heads up — pushed a small prototype for a stripe-oriented safetensors layout that stores zstd-compressed microchunks and supports on-the-fly decompression while streaming. Branch: feat/safestripe-zstd
Ravi K: Nice. What's the warmup model for this? eager hotfill, index-first, or manifestless streaming?
Sofia P: Prototype is manifestless streaming by default. The idea: client requests byte ranges for chunk stripes, server decompresses in-flight and feeds runtime KV loads. Aims to reduce storage IO for large rotated checkpoints.
Anya L: Two immediate tradeoffs: CPU cost of zstd decompression on the serving path, and memory pressure if we keep decompressed buffers pinned for KV pages. How are you addressing that?
Sofia P: We experimented with an LRU of decompressed pages + opportunistic re-compression to temp scratch if mem high. Also leverage hw-accelerated zstd where available.
Kevin M: Can you sketch the request flow? e.g. pseudocode for the streaming path so we can reason about backpressure.
Sofia P: Sure — rough flow:
```
Client -> Router -> WeightGateway: resolve shard stripe offsets
WeightGateway: issue range reads (compressed) from blobstore
Decompressor: incremental zstd streaming -> emit chunks
Loader: map emitted chunks into KV pages, touch GPU memory
Runtime: attach pages to model instance
```
Ravi K: How do you handle partial chunk failures? If a compressed microchunk read fails mid-stream, is there retry semantics or fallbacks?
Sofia P: Fallback order in prototype: 1) retry range read, 2) fall back to uncompressed sidecar if present, 3) fall back to index-first manifest/replica. Fail-open only as last resort.
Anya L: We should be explicit about alignment: decompressed output boundaries must match page boundaries or we get messy memcpy+slice overheads. Are microchunks aligned to 4KB/64KB pages?
Sofia P: Microchunk size configurable; default aligned to 64KB decompressed. That keeps GPU memcpy friendly and reduces reassembly work.
Kevin M: Telemetry hooks? We need CPU time per decompress, bytes read saved, extra latency percentiles, and memory pinned gauge. Also a metric for fallback rate to uncompressed.
Sofia P: Agreed — prototype emits metrics: decompress_cpu_ms, compressed_bytes_read, decompressed_bytes_emitted, pinned_pages, fallback_uncompressed_count. We'll add histograms for per-request latency.
Ravi K: What about caching semantics across requests and workers? If one worker decompresses stripe A and evicts it, can a nearby worker reuse the compressed blob instead of re-decompressing?
Sofia P: Plan: keep compressed-on-disk blobs in shared blobstore so re-read cost minimal, but decompressed cache is local. To avoid duplicate decompression hot loops, we have an in-memory singleflight per-stripe key with short TTL.
Anya L: Singleflight helps but watch thundering herd when stripe is large and many warmups request overlapping offsets. Need backpressure so loader advertises bytes accepted and decompressor respects it.
Sofia P: Loader advertises token window; decompressor runs at most N inflight chunks per model instance. Also added an optional prewarm coordinator that can schedule stripe decompression ahead of traffic.
Kevin M: Security/compliance note: compressed artifacts still need provenance and checksums. If we accept manifestless streaming we must embed a small compact header with version + checksum per stripe so we can verify before decompression.
Sofia P: Prototype embeds a 32b manifest header per stripe (version, zstd-level, checksum). Good call.
Ravi K: Ops: can we serve zstd stripes from cold NFS/slow object stores without blowing P95 latency? What SLOs do we expect?
Sofia P: Expectation: P95 for first-token if manifestless streaming = higher (e.g., 150–300ms depending on object store). With warm coordinator pre-decompress it's similar to uncompressed warmstart. We'll model tradeoffs in README.
Anya L: I worry about mixing quantized binary blobs with compressed stripes; quant formats expect exact layout. Need stable mapping from stripe->tensor offsets so quant loaders can map directly.
Sofia P: We keep an offset index per-shard (small sidecar) that maps tensor name -> list of stripe ranges. That index is small and fetched first (index-first warm path) for strict-map workloads.
Kevin M: Sounds good. One more ask: make the prototype opt-in via weight-source header so Dedicated/Private customers can disable on-the-fly zstd if they prefer deterministic performance.
Sofia P: Will do. Also adding feature flag and config knobs for microchunk size, singleflight TTL, decompress concurrency, and prewarm window.
loader-bot: Deployer: preview image built and pushed: ghcr.io/redwood/weights-gateway:feat-safestripe-zstd-20230922. Runbook: /dev/docs/safestripe-warmup.md
Ravi K: Thanks — next steps: 1) perf microbench showing CPU cost vs saved IO, 2) integration with warm coordinator, 3) add manifest header verification and metrics.
Sofia P: I'll open a follow-up RFC with numbers and a couple of config proposals. For now please try the branch and drop experiments in #eng-ml. :thumbsup:
